title: Su boregi
subtitle: Layered filo pastry with feta and parsley
excerpt: Su boregi is a Turkish borek made with filo pastry layered with a feta and parsley filling and baked in a deep tray until golden and crisp on top. It slices neatly into rectangles and is eaten warm or at room temperature as a brunch dish or part of a meze spread.
sourceNotes: Aylin Oney Tan, A Taste of Sun and Fire: Gaziantep Cookery (2014). Su boregi documented as a classic Turkish breakfast and brunch pastry. Claudia Roden, Arabesque (2005). Filo borek variations described across Turkey, Greece, and the Arab world.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the unbaked assembled borek, well-wrapped. Bake from frozen at 190 degrees for 50 to 55 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 24 hours ahead, cover, and refrigerate. Bake straight from the fridge, adding five minutes.

content.text: Su boregi is a Turkish layered pastry: sheets of filo brushed with butter and layered in a deep tray with a filling of crumbled feta and flat-leaf parsley. The result is crispy on top and bottom, with soft layers and a salty, savoury filling inside. It bakes in forty minutes and is cut into rectangles to serve. The name means 'water borek' after the traditional method of briefly boiling the pastry dough; using shop-bought filo avoids this step entirely.
Preheat the oven to 200 degrees. Mix {{feta}}, {{parsley-flat}}, beaten {{eggs}}, and {{black-pepper}} together in a bowl. The feta provides most of the salt; taste before adding more.
Brush a 30 x 20 cm baking dish with melted {{unsalted-butter}}. Lay two sheets of {{filo-pastry}} in the base, letting the edges overhang the sides. Brush generously with butter.
Add two more sheets of filo and brush with butter. Spread half the feta filling evenly over the surface.

Add two more sheets of buttered filo, then the remaining filling. Lay the final four to six sheets of filo on top, brushing each with butter. Fold any overhanging edges over the top and brush the surface with more butter. Scatter {{sesame-seeds}} over the top if using.

Score the top layers lightly into rectangles with a sharp knife (do not cut all the way through). Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is deeply golden and crisp. Leave to rest for ten minutes before cutting.

items.symptom: The top layers are golden but the interior is still doughy
items.cause: Oven temperature too high, cooking the outside before the heat penetrates
items.fix: Bake at 180 degrees fan for the last fifteen minutes if the top is browning too fast. Cover loosely with foil to finish.

items.cause: Filo dries out quickly at room temperature
items.fix: Keep unused sheets under a damp cloth while you work. Work quickly and brush with butter as soon as a sheet is laid.
Drain the feta in a sieve for twenty minutes before mixing. Press it lightly to remove excess liquid.

items.symptom: The bottom is pale and not crispy
items.cause: Not enough butter on the base layers, or dish not hot when the pastry went in
items.fix: Brush the base layers generously. Preheating the baking tray under the dish also helps the base cook.

content.text: Borek is the broad Turkish category of layered or rolled pastry dishes with savoury fillings, eaten at breakfast, as a snack, or as part of a meze spread. Su boregi, the layered tray version with feta and parsley, is one of the most common at home and in pastry shops across Turkey. It appears at breakfast tables, wedding spreads, and office canteens. The filling can vary: spinach and feta, meat, or potato are also common. Filo-based borek is closely related to the Greek spanakopita and the Balkan burek; all share an Ottoman pastry heritage.
